::: {.callout-note title="Calculations – 🧪 OD" collapse="true"}
## Purpose

We need to provide the same amount of carbon to Daphnia otherwise a diet could simply be supplying more or less food overall, confounding food *quantity* with the food *quality*. Optical density (OD) at 480 nm is a fast proxy for how much algal carbon is in a culture, but the relationship between OD and carbon content is species-specific and must be calibrated for each algal species.

This analysis fits that calibration for *Microcystis aeruginosa* and *Nannochloropsis limnetica*: a linear equation converting an OD<sub>480</sub> reading of either species, grown in zoo-COMBO medium, into the corresponding carbon concentration (mg C/L). Once fitted, the equation lets the volume of culture needed for a given carbon dose be read straight off a quick OD measurement.

## Methods

### Dilution series and optical density

For each species, a dilution series was prepared in zoo-COMBO medium (COMBO without nitrogen and phosphorus, which halts algal growth) — *Microcystis aeruginosa* at 0, 10, 25, 35, 50, 75, and 100% of the stock culture, and *Nannochloropsis limnetica* at 0, 10, 25, 50, 75, and 100%. Each dilution's OD<sub>480</sub> was read on a spectrophotometer (raw data in [2_data/01_unprocessed/01_OD](../2_data/01_unprocessed/01_OD)).

### Carbon content

A matched volume of each dilution was filtered onto a drying plate — one plate per species — dried in a 24-well plate, both species packaged together in a 96-well plate and sent together to Dominik Martin-Creuzburg's lab (Bad Saarow, Germany) for carbon and nitrogen analysis. Data came back with filters from an unrelated project (Claudia's), which are excluded. Filters flagged as compromised — accidentally touched during handling, burnt during analysis, or lost — are excluded as well.

### Calibration

Carbon mass is converted to a concentration (mg C/L) by dividing the measured carbon (mg) by the volume of culture filtered (mL). That concentration is then regressed linearly against the matching OD<sub>480</sub> reading, separately for each species:

$$C_{mg/L} = \text{intercept} + \text{slope} \times OD_{480}$$

```{r}
#| label: data_prep
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)

OD_data_dir <- "../2_data/01_unprocessed/01_OD"

# ----- Microcystis aeruginosa: OD + volume ------ #

Microcystis_volume_added <- read.csv(file.path(OD_data_dir, "Microcystis_volume.csv"), fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
Microcystis_OD <- read.csv(file.path(OD_data_dir, "Microcystis_OD.csv"), fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")

Microcystis_volume_and_OD <- left_join(
  Microcystis_volume_added,
  Microcystis_OD,
  by = c("species", "medium", "percentage")
) %>%
select(-c("comment", "position_drying_plate"))

# ----- Nannochloropsis limnetica: OD + volume ------ #

Nannochloropsis_volume_added <- read.csv(file.path(OD_data_dir, "Nannochloropsis_volume.csv"), fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM") %>%
mutate(problem = "no")
Nannochloropsis_OD <- read.csv(file.path(OD_data_dir, "Nannochloropsis_OD.csv"), fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")

Nannochloropsis_volume_and_OD <- left_join(
  Nannochloropsis_volume_added,
  Nannochloropsis_OD,
  by = c("species", "medium", "percentage")
) %>%
select(-c("position_drying_plate"))

# ----- Carbon content ------ #
# "plate" holds the elemental-analyser plate label. Rows from the unrelated
# project were run on plate "Claudia" and are dropped here so only this
# calibration's samples remain.

Microcystis_Nannochlaropsis_C <- read.csv(file.path(OD_data_dir, "Microcystis_Nannochlaropsis_C.csv"), fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM") %>%
filter(!plate == "Claudia") %>%
select(position_C_analysis_plate = plate, C_mg = C..mg.) %>%
mutate(
  position_C_analysis_plate = str_extract(str_trim(position_C_analysis_plate), "^[A-Z]\\d+"),
  C_mg = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(C_mg)) # non-numeric placeholders (e.g. "sample lost") become NA
)

# ----- Merge tables ------ #
# problem != "no" rows (a touched or burnt filter) and unmatched/NA carbon
# readings are dropped, since neither gives a usable calibration point.

Volume_and_OD <- bind_rows(Microcystis_volume_and_OD, Nannochloropsis_volume_and_OD)

Volume_OD_and_C <- left_join(
  Volume_and_OD,
  Microcystis_Nannochlaropsis_C,
  by = "position_C_analysis_plate"
) %>%
filter(!is.na(C_mg), problem != "yes") %>%
select(species, percentage, volume_added_ml, OD_480_nm, C_mg)
```

```{r}
#| label: carbon_concentration

species_OD_C <- Volume_OD_and_C %>%
mutate(C_mg_per_L = C_mg / volume_added_ml * 1000) %>%
select(species, OD_480_nm, C_mg_per_L)
```

## Results

### Microcystis aeruginosa

```{r}
#| label: microcystis_calibration

m_aeruginosa_OD_C <- species_OD_C %>%
filter(species == "microcystis_aeruginosa")

m_aeruginosa_lm <- lm(C_mg_per_L ~ OD_480_nm, data = m_aeruginosa_OD_C)
m_aeruginosa_intercept <- coef(m_aeruginosa_lm)[["(Intercept)"]]
m_aeruginosa_slope <- coef(m_aeruginosa_lm)[["OD_480_nm"]]
m_aeruginosa_r_squared <- summary(m_aeruginosa_lm)$r.squared

cat(sprintf(
  "Microcystis aeruginosa: C_mg_per_L = %.2f + %.2f * OD_480_nm (R2 = %.3f)\n",
  m_aeruginosa_intercept, m_aeruginosa_slope, m_aeruginosa_r_squared
))

ggplot(aes(x = OD_480_nm, y = C_mg_per_L), data = m_aeruginosa_OD_C) +
geom_point() +
geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x)
```

### Nannochloropsis limnetica

```{r}
#| label: nannochloropsis_calibration

n_limnetica_OD_C <- species_OD_C %>%
filter(species == "nannochloropsis_limnetica")

n_limnetica_lm <- lm(C_mg_per_L ~ OD_480_nm, data = n_limnetica_OD_C)
n_limnetica_intercept <- coef(n_limnetica_lm)[["(Intercept)"]]
n_limnetica_slope <- coef(n_limnetica_lm)[["OD_480_nm"]]
n_limnetica_r_squared <- summary(n_limnetica_lm)$r.squared

cat(sprintf(
  "Nannochloropsis limnetica: C_mg_per_L = %.2f + %.2f * OD_480_nm (R2 = %.3f)\n",
  n_limnetica_intercept, n_limnetica_slope, n_limnetica_r_squared
))

ggplot(aes(x = OD_480_nm, y = C_mg_per_L), data = n_limnetica_OD_C) +
geom_point() +
geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x)
```

## Use

These two equations are what let a single OD<sub>480</sub> reading of a treatment's phytoplankton culture be converted, on any given feeding day, into a volume of that culture to add so that every diet receives the same carbon dose. Holding food quantity constant this way is what lets differences in *Daphnia* and *Chaoborus* performance across treatments be attributed to food quality and toxin exposure, rather than to how much food they were fed.

## Save parameters

```{r}
#| label: save_OD_parameters

Nannochloropsis_OD_to_C_slope <- round(n_limnetica_slope, 2)
Nannochloropsis_OD_to_C_intercept <- round(n_limnetica_intercept, 2)
Microcystis_OD_to_C_slope <- round(m_aeruginosa_slope, 2)
Microcystis_OD_to_C_intercept <- round(m_aeruginosa_intercept, 2)
```

calculations/food_calculator.qmd embeds a standalone Shinylive app that runs client-side in the reader's browser, with no access to this R session or to the repository's data files at render time. The snapshot below is how it stays in sync with the calibration above without values being copied over by hand: re-rendering this file (or the master document) refreshes the snapshot, and re-rendering food_calculator.qmd then bakes the refreshed numbers into the embedded app.

```{r}
#| label: save_food_calculator_parameters

## Diet_*_fraction (source of truth for diet composition, see 4_parameters.qmd) are
## vectors, so every value is deparsed to an R literal (e.g. "c(0.5, 0, 0, 0)") and the
## whole value column is stored as text; food_calculator.qmd splices these literals
## straight into the app's R source, so a scalar's deparsed text ("0.8") assigns the
## same way a vector's ("c(0.5, 0, 0, 0)") does.
Food_calculator_parameters <- data.frame(
  name = c(
    "Large_jar_liquid_litres",
    "Daphnia_algae_C_ad_libitum_mg_per_L_per_day",
    "N_days_per_feeding_event",
    "extra_food_ratio",
    "Diet_Microcystis_fraction",
    "Diet_Synechococcus_fraction",
    "Diet_Nannochloropsis_fraction",
    "Diet_Tetradesmus_fraction",
    "Tetradesmus_OD_to_C_slope",
    "Tetradesmus_OD_to_C_intercept",
    "Synechococcus_OD_to_C_slope",
    "Synechococcus_OD_to_C_intercept",
    "Microcystis_OD_to_C_slope",
    "Microcystis_OD_to_C_intercept",
    "Nannochloropsis_OD_to_C_slope",
    "Nannochloropsis_OD_to_C_intercept"
  ),
  value = c(
    deparse(Large_jar_liquid_litres),
    deparse(Daphnia_algae_C_ad_libitum_mg_per_L_per_day),
    deparse(N_days_per_feeding_event),
    deparse(extra_food_ratio),
    deparse(Diet_Microcystis_fraction),
    deparse(Diet_Synechococcus_fraction),
    deparse(Diet_Nannochloropsis_fraction),
    deparse(Diet_Tetradesmus_fraction),
    deparse(Tetradesmus_OD_to_C_slope),
    deparse(Tetradesmus_OD_to_C_intercept),
    deparse(Synechococcus_OD_to_C_slope),
    deparse(Synechococcus_OD_to_C_intercept),
    deparse(Microcystis_OD_to_C_slope),
    deparse(Microcystis_OD_to_C_intercept),
    deparse(Nannochloropsis_OD_to_C_slope),
    deparse(Nannochloropsis_OD_to_C_intercept)
  )
)

write.csv(
  Food_calculator_parameters,
  file.path("calculations", "food_calculator_parameters.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
